issues.watering-log/long-bed-name-table-overflo: At 375px, a long unbroken bed name makes the watering tables on /waterings and the dashboard wider than the viewport, causing horizontal scrolling.
issues.watering-log/hung-filter-stale-rows: On /waterings, when the request for a newly chosen bed filter hangs, the page stays on 'Loading waterings…' and keeps listing other beds' rows under the selected bed.
issues.watering-log/shared-watering-busy-state: On /beds a single shared wateringBedId/notice/error state means starting 'Water now' on a second bed re-enables the first bed's button mid-request, allowing duplicate waterings and lost messages.
issues.watering-log/water-now-no-progress-label: On /beds, clicking 'Water now' while that bed's past-watering form is open disables the button but keeps the label 'Water now' with no 'Watering…' feedback.
issues.watering-log/success-shown-when-refresh-: On /beds, after 'Water now' succeeds but the follow-up beds refresh fails, the success notice is shown while 'Last watered' stays stale with no error.
issues.watering-log/refresh-failure-replaces-be: On /beds, if GET /api/beds fails after a successful 'Water now', the bed list and success notice are replaced by 'Could not load beds.' with no retry.
issues.watering-log/filter-late-response-race: On /waterings, quickly switching the bed filter on a slow connection may let an earlier response overwrite the newer filter's results because there is no request ordering.
issues.watering-log/malformed-watering-fields-r: Waterings whose fields are null or malformed render as-is on /waterings and the dashboard (e.g. 'Never', blank bed, 'x L', raw 'garbage' date) instead of placeholders.

harvest-stats/blank-date-silent-default.sentence: On /stats, clearing the From or To field drops the parameter so the server silently uses this year's 1 Jan or 31 Dec, leaving the field blank while results use another range or showing 'The From date must be on or before the To date.'; triggered by clearing a date field, especially with the other date outside this year.
harvest-stats/blank-date-silent-default.evidence: Code: stats.vue omits empty from/to from the API query, and stats.py replaces a missing value with this year's 1 Jan / 31 Dec (date_from or year_start). In the running app, signed in as demo: (1) /stats?from=2025-01-01&to=2025-12-31 showed '1 harvest from 1 Jan 2025 to 31 Dec 2025'. After clearing From, the URL became ?to=2025-12-31, the From input was empty, and the page showed the alert 'The From date must be on or before the To date.' even though no From date was entered. (2) /stats?from=2024-01-01&to=2026-06-30, then clearing From: the From input stayed blank while the results line said '1 harvest from 1 Jan 2026 to 30 Jun 2026'. The range was quietly narrowed to this year with no message. (3) From=2026-03-01 with To cleared: results ran to 31 Dec 2026 while the To field was blank. A blank field is neither refused with a clear reason nor treated as open-ended, so what the user sees in the form does not match the range the results use.

harvest-stats/dashboard-top-plant-ambigu.sentence: On the dashboard, the 'Top plant this year' card shows only the plant name and links to /stats, so same-named plants cannot be told apart; triggered by having two plants with the same name and viewing the dashboard.
harvest-stats/dashboard-top-plant-ambigu.evidence: Signed in as the demo user. Added a second plant through the API: 'Tomato' (variety 'Gardeners Delight', id 4), alongside the existing 'Tomato' Sungold (id 1), and logged a 2000 g harvest for it on 2026-08-01. GET /api/dashboard/summary then returned top_plant 'Tomato', top_plant_id 4, top_plant_grams 2000. On the dashboard at http://localhost:3794/ the 'Top plant this year' card showed only 'Tomato' / '2 kg harvested'. Its link, labelled 'View top plant this year', points to /stats, not /plants/4. index.vue only reads summary.top_plant and top_plant_grams; top_plant_id is never used, and SummaryOut has no variety field. So there is no way to tell which Tomato is meant. The stats page does show ' · variety' next to plant names, so the app treats same-named plants as needing the variety everywhere except this card. The test plant and harvest were deleted afterwards.

harvest-stats/date-fields-ignore-url-cha.sentence: On /stats, the date fields are read from the URL only at setup, so clicking the Stats nav link or using back/forward while on the page changes the URL but not the fields or data; triggered by picking a custom range and then navigating to /stats within the app.
harvest-stats/date-fields-ignore-url-cha.evidence: Signed in as demo user and opened /stats: From 2026-01-01, To 2026-12-31, '5 harvests from 1 Jan 2026 to 31 Dec 2026'. Set From to 2025-01-01: URL became /stats?from=2025-01-01, '6 harvests from 1 Jan 2025 to 31 Dec 2026', 'This year' button shown. Clicked the 'Stats' main-nav link: URL changed to /stats (no query) but From stayed 2025-01-01, the results still said '6 harvests from 1 Jan 2025...' and the 'This year' button was still shown. Then pushed /stats?from=2023-03-01 with the in-app router: URL updated, fields and data still showed 2025-01-01. Code agrees: stats.vue sets dateFrom/dateTo from route.query only once at setup, the only watcher goes from the refs to router.replace, and NuxtPage has no page-key, so the component is reused. The URL and the page drift apart, and the Stats nav link no longer resets to this year.

harvest-stats/empty-months-omitted.sentence: On /stats, the weight-by-month table only has columns for months with harvests, so empty months in the chosen range are silently skipped; triggered by choosing a range that includes months without harvests.
harvest-stats/empty-months-omitted.evidence: Signed in through POST /api/auth/login as the demo user. GET /api/stats/harvests with the default range (2026-01-01..2026-12-31) returned months ['2026-06','2026-07','2026-08','2026-09']. With from=2025-01-01&to=2026-12-31 it returned ['2025-08','2026-06','2026-07','2026-08','2026-09'], jumping from Aug 2025 straight to Jun 2026. In backend/routers/stats.py, months is built only from the grouped result rows (months = sorted({row['month'] for row in rows})), so the range's calendar months are never filled in. frontend/app/pages/stats.vue makes one table column for each entry in stats.months and adds no gap months. So the per-month table does not cover the chosen range: empty months, including gaps in the middle, disappear without any sign, and that misrepresents 'weight per month for the chosen range'. I did not check the rendered page in the browser.

harvest-stats/long-plant-name-narrow-lay.sentence: On /stats at 375 px width, a long unbroken plant name is truncated in Best plants and the nowrap table row header pushes all month and total columns out of view (or makes the page scroll sideways); triggered by creating a plant with a very long name and viewing the page on a narrow screen.
harvest-stats/long-plant-name-narrow-lay.evidence: Used the API to create plant id 4 with an 80-character unbroken name ('Supercalifragilisticexpialidociousbeanstalkwithaverylongnamethatneverbreaksxxx'; 80 is the schema maximum) and a 900 kg harvest on 2026-11-01. Signed in through the UI and opened /stats at a 375x800 viewport. Best plants No. 1 shows 'Supercalifragilis…'. Its .stat__value has white-space: nowrap and text-overflow: ellipsis (scrollWidth 1257 vs clientWidth 290) and no title attribute, so the full name can't be read there. In the table, the new rule .stats-table th[scope=row] { white-space: nowrap } makes the plant column about 595 px wide inside a .table-scroll that is 309 px wide (scrollWidth 1100). Every month header (Jun to Nov 2026) and the Total column start at x>=628 and are outside the visible box, so on load you see only plant names and no weights, including in the Total row. The page itself does not scroll sideways (document scrollWidth 375), which matches the reports. Screenshot: scratch/playwright/stats375.png. Note: the ellipsis style on .stat__value already existed (dashboard stat cards); the nowrap row header is new in this change. The table can still be scrolled sideways, so the data is reachable but hidden at phone width.

harvest-stats/malformed-response-crash.sentence: On /stats, a 200 response with a malformed, non-JSON, empty or null-field body throws an uncaught TypeError, leaving the page stuck on 'Loading stats…' over old data (or not rendering at all on client navigation); triggered by mocking /api/stats/harvests with such a body and changing a date or navigating to Stats.
harvest-stats/malformed-response-crash.evidence: Signed in as the demo user. (1) On the dashboard I routed /api/stats/harvests to return 200 {"plants":null} and clicked the nav link 'Stats'. The URL changed to /stats, but #main still showed the Dashboard content, and an 'Error details' dialog appeared with 'TypeError Cannot read properties of null (reading 'length')' (also caught as a pageerror). The Stats page never rendered. (2) I loaded /stats normally, then routed the endpoint to return 200 with months:[{month:null}], plants:[{monthly_grams:null}] and top_plants:null, and set From to 2026-07-01. The URL became /stats?from=2026-07-01. A pageerror and an error dialog showed 'Cannot read properties of null (reading 'slice')'. The page stayed on 'Loading stats…' while still showing the old 1 Jan–31 Dec 2026 table and best plants (Courgette 1.2 kg and so on) under the new range. Cause in code: stats.vue uses the useApiFetch data directly with no shape checks (stats.plants.length, formatMonth(month.month), and so on), so the 'Could not load harvest stats.' AlertMessage never appears.

harvest-stats/malformed-response-renders.sentence: On /stats, a stats response with null or missing fields renders as 'undefined/null harvests from – to –' with empty sections instead of an error state; triggered by mocking /api/stats/harvests with null fields.
harvest-stats/malformed-response-renders.evidence: Reproduced: signed in as the demo user, used Playwright page.route to make GET /api/stats/harvests return 200 with date_from/date_to/total_grams null, harvest_count missing, months [] and one plant with null name/totals, then clicked Stats in the nav. The main text read 'undefined harvests from – to – Best plants Weight by plant and month – total ... PLANT TOTAL – Total –', which matches the reports. This is not a real defect, though. The backend endpoint is declared with response_model=HarvestStatsOut (backend/routers/stats.py:40), and that Pydantic model makes date_from/date_to dates, total_grams/harvest_count ints and months/plants/top_plants lists, all required (backend/schemas.py:155-162). So the real API cannot send this payload; it only appears when the response is faked in the browser. No other page in the app checks response shapes either: useApiFetch is a plain useFetch wrapper and every page trusts the typed API. The request asked for nothing about handling malformed responses. The page does show its error state for real failures (statsError leads to AlertMessage), and nulls are shown as '–' instead of crashing. At most this is a hardening nicety.

harvest-stats/raw-validation-message.sentence: On /stats, an invalid date (e.g. ?from=2026-02-30 or a five-digit year) shows the raw validation text 'Query.from: Input should be a valid date or datetime…' and the date input appears blank; triggered by opening such a URL or typing such a date.
harvest-stats/raw-validation-message.evidence: Logged in as the demo user via POST /api/auth/login. GET /api/stats/harvests?from=2026-02-30 returned 422 with a pydantic detail: loc ['query','from'], msg 'Input should be a valid date or datetime, day value is outside expected range'. The router (backend/routers/stats.py) declares the parameter as `date | None` and does not handle bad dates itself. Fetching the page http://localhost:3795/stats?from=2026-02-30 with the session cookie gave SSR HTML containing <div class="alert alert--error" role="alert">Query.from: Input should be a valid date or datetime, day value is outside expected range. The raw field path and pydantic wording reach the user, unlike the friendly message the app wrote for the from>to case. The input renders as <input id="stats-from" value="2026-02-30" type="date">. A native date input cannot show an impossible date, so it looks blank while the error refers to it.

harvest-stats/stale-summary-on-error.sentence: On /stats, after a successful load, a failed request for a new range leaves the old range's '<n> harvests from ... to ...' summary line visible next to the error; triggered by making the next stats request fail after changing dates.
harvest-stats/stale-summary-on-error.evidence: Signed in as demo user, opened /stats: summary read '5 harvests from 1 Jan 2026 to 31 Dec 2026'. Routed **/api/stats/harvests** to return 500 {detail:'Injected 500'}, then filled From = 2026-07-01 (URL became /stats?from=2026-07-01). Page then showed 'Injected 500' alert AND still the summary '5 harvests from 1 Jan 2026 to 31 Dec 2026' for a range no longer selected. Cause in frontend/app/pages/stats.vue: loadStats catch sets statsError but leaves stats.value as the old data, and the results-count template uses `v-else-if="stats"` with no statsError check, so stale rangeText renders beside the error.

harvest-stats/stats-no-retry-after-error.sentence: On /stats, the error state shows only a message with no Retry button, so recovering requires changing a date or reloading; triggered by making /api/stats/harvests fail.
harvest-stats/stats-no-retry-after-error.evidence: Signed in as the demo user, routed GET **/api/stats/harvests** to 500 {"detail":"boom"}, then clicked Stats in the main nav. /stats showed the From/To fields (2026-01-01 / 2026-12-31) and a single alert reading 'boom'. There was no retry button; the only buttons were Sign out and, after changing the range, 'This year'. So the behaviour is real. But the request (.rough-ride/specs/request.txt) does not ask for a retry action, and no page in the app has one: beds.vue, tasks.vue, plants/index.vue, plants/new.vue and the dashboard (index.vue) all show load failures as an AlertMessage with only text. AlertMessage.vue is just a slot with no action. stats.vue follows the app's existing pattern. The page also re-fetches when a date changes, so recovery without a reload works. Adding Retry would be a nice extra, not a defect in this change.

harvest-stats/stats-no-timeout.sentence: On /stats, a stats request that never answers leaves 'Loading stats…' on screen indefinitely (often above the previous range's results) with no timeout or error; triggered by making /api/stats/harvests hang and opening the page or changing a date.
harvest-stats/stats-no-timeout.evidence: Reproduced: signed in as demo, opened /stats (default 2026 range, 2.6 kg table), routed **/api/stats/harvests** to never respond, set From to 2026-07-01. After 20 s the page still showed 'Loading stats…' above the old 1 Jan-31 Dec 2026 table and Best plants, with no error or retry. However this is the app's existing convention, not something the change introduced: the app has no request timeouts anywhere (useApiFetch/useApiClient in composables/useApi.ts set no timeout; grep finds no timeout/AbortController in the frontend), and stats.vue copies the pre-existing plants/index.vue pattern ('Loading plants…' while status==='pending', previous results stay visible). Doing the same to the unchanged /plants page (hang **/api/plants**, type 'tom' in search) gives the same result: 'Loading plants…' forever above the old, unfiltered list. The request did not ask for timeout or retry handling. The new page matches how the rest of the app is meant to work. Real errors (non-hang) are handled by the AlertMessage branch.

plant-journal/body-limit-counts-utf16-un.sentence: The journal entry form's maxlength and character counter count UTF-16 units, so emoji count double (about 250 fit) and server-accepted 500-emoji entries cannot be edited and saved.
plant-journal/body-limit-counts-utf16-un.evidence: Code: JournalEntryForm.vue uses :maxlength=500, remaining = 500 - form.body.length, and validate() checks form.body.trim().length > 500, all in UTF-16 units. The server (Pydantic max_length=500) and the SQLite CHECK length(body) both count code points. In the running app (signed in as the demo user): (1) a POST /api/journal with 500 x '🌱' returned 201, so the server accepts it. (2) On /plants/2 I inserted 300 '🌱' into the new-entry textarea. Only 250 emoji (500 UTF-16 units) were kept and the counter read '0 characters left'. (3) I clicked Edit on the 500-emoji entry. The edit textarea held 500 code points (1000 units) and the counter read '-500 characters left'. Clicking Save showed the client error 'Keep the entry to 500 characters.' and sent no PUT/PATCH request, so an entry the server accepted cannot be saved after editing. I deleted the test entry afterwards.

plant-journal/control-chars-accepted-in-.sentence: POST /api/journal accepts and stores control characters such as an embedded NUL in the entry text, which are later rendered in the feed.
plant-journal/control-chars-accepted-in-.evidence: Reproduced the behaviour: after logging in as demo, POST /api/journal {plant_id:2, entry_on:'2026-11-01', body:'a\u0000b\u0007c\u001bd'} returned 201, and GET /api/journal returned the body unchanged. The code agrees: JournalEntryIn.body is only Field(min_length=1, max_length=500) with str_strip_whitespace, and there is no control-character check. But this matches how the whole app already handles text, and it is not something the journal change introduced or that the request asks for. POST /api/plants with name 'x\u0000y' is also accepted (201) and stored as-is, and on main the bed/plant schemas (name/notes) have no control-character filtering either. The request only says 'a text of up to 500 characters', and that limit is enforced (blank text gets a 422). A gardener cannot normally type NUL into the textarea. The text is shown through Vue text interpolation, which escapes it, so there is no injection risk. Test entry 4 and test plant 4 were deleted afterwards.

plant-journal/create-retry-duplicate-ent.sentence: POST /api/journal has no idempotency key or dedupe, so retrying Add entry on the plant page after a lost or timed-out response creates a duplicate entry.
plant-journal/create-retry-duplicate-ent.evidence: Reproduced the mechanics: signed in as demo, opened /plants/2 (Courgette), and used page.route to let the first POST /api/journal reach the server (route.fetch) and then abort it client-side as 'timedout'. The form showed 'The garden server could not be reached.' and kept the text. Clicking Add entry again sent a second POST, and GET /api/journal?q=<text> returned two identical entries (ids 4 and 5); both are visible on the page, so the user can see and delete the extra one. The code matches: create_entry in backend/routers/journal.py inserts unconditionally and addEntry() sends no request key. But the request (dated entries, newest first, edit/delete, Journal page with search, counts) never asks for idempotent creates. The app's existing create endpoints (e.g. create_harvest in backend/routers/harvests.py) work the same way, and the codebase has no idempotency or dedupe anywhere. The duplicate needs a response lost after the server commits, and the result is visible and easy to undo. This is ordinary non-idempotent POST behaviour consistent with the app's design, not a regression or something the feature should have handled. (The side note about a retried delete giving 404 is the same lost-response scenario.)

plant-journal/delete-of-missing-entry-er.sentence: Deleting an entry that is already gone (second tab or retried delete) returns 404 'Journal entry not found.' as an error and the stale entry stays listed because the list only refreshes on success.
plant-journal/delete-of-missing-entry-er.evidence: Reproduced: signed in, opened /plants/1 (journal entries 2 and 1), deleted entry 2 through the API (204), then clicked Delete on entry 2 in the open page and confirmed. The DELETE returned 404 {"detail":"Journal entry not found."}. The page showed 'Journal entry not found.' and the entry stayed listed until reload, while the server list was [1,3]. Code: removeEntry (frontend/app/pages/plants/[id].vue:128) refreshes only on success, and delete_entry (backend/routers/journal.py:85) returns 404 for a missing id. But this matches the app's existing delete convention exactly: the pre-existing harvest delete in the initial commit (removeHarvest plus delete_harvest, and also delete_plant) does the same thing (404 for a missing id, error shown, no refresh on failure). The error message is accurate and no data is lost or wrongly changed; the only effect is a stale view after another tab or lost response changed the data, and a reload fixes it. The app has no live sync anywhere, and the request does not ask for idempotent deletes or cross-tab consistency. So the new feature follows the established design and does not introduce a regression.

plant-journal/edited-label-missing-same-.sentence: Editing a journal entry within the same second it was created shows no 'edited' label because timestamps have one-second resolution.
plant-journal/edited-label-missing-same-.evidence: The mechanism is real. JournalEntryItem.vue:20 sets edited = updated_at !== created_at, and both columns are written with SQLite datetime('now') (journal.py update_entry, db.py defaults), which only stores whole seconds. Via the API: POST /api/journal created entry 4 at created_at=updated_at='2026-11-12 18:42:53'. An immediate PUT returned the changed body but updated_at was still '18:42:53'. A PUT 1.5s later gave updated_at '18:42:55'. In the UI (Playwright on /plants/2), a script that added an entry, clicked Edit, changed the text and clicked Save entry took 168 ms in total, and the edited entry showed no 'edited' label. The entry edited 2 s after creation did show it. However, the request never asks for an 'edited' label; it is an extra. The only way to miss it is to finish an edit within the same wall-clock second as creation, which a person opening the editor, typing and saving cannot realistically do. Edits made at human speed are labelled correctly. Second-precision timestamps are also the convention for every table in the app (plants.updated_at works the same way). So this is a theoretical edge case, not a defect a user or the request would reject.

plant-journal/failed-refresh-after-add-h.sentence: On the plant page, if adding an entry succeeds but the following journal refresh fails, the whole list is replaced by a load error with no retry while the badge count increases.
plant-journal/failed-refresh-after-add-h.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /plants/3 (Lettuce). Before: badge '1 entry' and one entry listed ('14 May 2026 Thinned the seedlings.' with Edit/Delete). Used a Playwright route that let POST /api/journal through and returned 503 for every later GET /api/journal. Added the entry 'Verify refresh failure entry'. After: POST succeeded, the form was cleared ('500 characters left'), the badge changed to '2 entries', and the entry list was gone (0 list items). The only thing left in its place was the load-error alert (it showed the mocked 503 detail text; without a detail it falls back to 'Could not load the journal.'). The only button left in the section was 'Add entry', so there was no retry control. Code cause: in pages/plants/[id].vue, addEntry calls refreshPlantAndJournal(), which refreshes the plant and the journal together. The plant refresh succeeds, so the count goes up. The journal useFetch fails, and Nuxt 4 resets its data to undefined, so the template condition `v-if="journal && journal.length"` hides the list. AlertMessage has no retry slot or action, so the initial-load failure has no retry either.

plant-journal/feed-long-plant-name-overf.sentence: On /journal at 375 px, a long unbroken plant name in the feed item link has no wrapping rule and makes the page scroll sideways.
plant-journal/feed-long-plant-name-overf.evidence: The backend allows plant names up to 80 characters (PlantIn.name max_length=80). Through the API I created plant 4, named 'Supercalifragilistic' x4 (80 characters, no spaces), in bed 1, and added one journal entry to it. I signed in in Playwright at a 375x800 viewport and opened /journal. document.documentElement.scrollWidth was 679 while clientWidth was 375, and html/body overflow-x was 'visible', so the page scrolls sideways. The computed style of A.journal-feed__plant showed overflow-wrap:normal and word-break:normal, and the link was 629 px wide. The elements sticking out past the viewport were LI.journal-feed__item (right edge 679), DIV.journal-entry__head, A.journal-feed__plant and P.journal-entry__body (right edge 662); the body is only pushed wider by its card. In main.css only .journal-entry__body gets overflow-wrap:anywhere. .journal-feed__plant has no wrapping rule. After I deleted the test plant (204), /journal went back to scrollWidth 375 = clientWidth 375. This is a valid 80-character name and it breaks the mobile layout of the new page.

plant-journal/implausible-old-dates-acce.sentence: POST/PUT /api/journal accepts implausible dates such as 0001-01-01, which are then shown as '1 Jan 1'.
plant-journal/implausible-old-dates-acce.evidence: Reproduced via API as demo user: POST /api/journal {plant_id:2, entry_on:'0001-01-01'} -> 201 (id 4); PUT /api/journal/4 entry_on '0001-01-02' -> 200. Test data deleted afterwards (204). However the request only asks for 'a date and a text of up to 500 characters' and specifies no minimum date. JournalEntryIn (backend/schemas.py:107-116) copies the existing, unchanged HarvestIn convention from main: only future dates are refused ('cannot be in the future'), with no lower bound. The pre-existing harvests endpoint behaves the same way: POST /api/harvests harvested_on '0001-01-01' -> 201 (deleted afterwards). So accepting very old dates follows the app's established date-validation design and is not something the change introduced or that the request rules out. A sensible lower bound would be a nice improvement, but it is not a defect in this change.

plant-journal/journal-load-error-no-retr.sentence: When GET /api/journal fails, the /journal page and the plant detail journal section show only 'Could not load the journal.' with no Retry control, requiring a reload or search edit to recover.
plant-journal/journal-load-error-no-retr.evidence: Reproduced in the running app: signed in as the demo user, made every GET to **/api/journal** return 500 with the Playwright route, then moved around client-side. On /journal, main showed only the error text from the API detail ('boom') and had no buttons. On /plants/2 the Journal section showed the error, the only button was 'Add entry', and there was no retry. Code agrees: journal.vue never takes refresh from useApiFetch, and the journal AlertMessage in [id].vue has no action. AlertMessage is just a slot. But this is how the whole app already handles load errors, from the original commit: no page in main has a retry control (git grep -i retry main finds nothing). Plants index, beds and tasks all show a bare AlertMessage on load failure. I checked in the browser: with GET /api/plants failing, /plants showed only the error and no buttons in main. With GET /api/tasks failing, /tasks showed the error plus only its normal form and filter buttons. The request does not ask for retry controls. The journal views follow the existing pattern, so this is not a regression or a gap against the request.

plant-journal/journal-requests-no-timeou.sentence: Journal fetches and mutations set no timeout, so when the API hangs the Add/Save button stays disabled on 'Saving…' or /journal stays on 'Loading entries…' indefinitely.
plant-journal/journal-requests-no-timeou.evidence: Reproduced the behaviour: signed in as the demo user, opened /plants/2, used Playwright page.route to make POST /api/journal hang, typed an entry and clicked 'Add entry'. After 14 s the button still said 'Saving…' and was disabled, with no error. However, this is not something the change introduced. composables/useApi.ts (useApiClient/useApiFetch, $fetch.create with no timeout) is unchanged from main (git diff main --stat does not list it), and nothing in the app sets a request timeout (grep finds no 'timeout'). Control test with an existing feature: on the same page, I made the existing plant edit save (PUT /api/plants/2) hang and clicked Save. After 14 s it also stayed on 'Saving…'. Beds and harvests use the same pattern. The request says nothing about timeouts, and the '10 seconds' expectation in the reports comes from nowhere in the request or the codebase. The journal code follows the app's existing request handling, so this is the app's design (any problem is app-wide and predates the change), not a defect in this change. The idempotency point in report 3 is also beyond the request.

plant-journal/long-search-raw-validation.sentence: Typing more than 80 characters into the /journal search box (no maxlength) makes the API return 422 and the page replaces results with a raw 'String should have at most 80 characters' message.
plant-journal/long-search-raw-validation.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /journal. Typed 81 'a' characters into the Search input (#journal-search). The input took all 81 characters and has no maxlength attribute. The URL changed to ?q=<81 a>, the results area disappeared, and the page body showed only 'Query.q: String should have at most 80 characters' (the console logged one error). In the code, backend/routers/journal.py declares q: str = Query(default='', max_length=80), so the API returns a 422. pages/journal.vue sends the trimmed search value straight to the API, does not limit the input length, and shows apiErrorMessage(loadError), which turns the FastAPI validation detail into 'Query.q: <msg>'. The user gets a raw, technical validation message in place of results, with no maxlength and no friendly explanation.

plant-journal/malformed-journal-response.sentence: When GET /api/journal returns a non-list body (object, string, HTML), the Journal page or plant journal section shows blank '–' entries or an empty/no-match state instead of a load error.
plant-journal/malformed-journal-response.evidence: Signed in as the demo user, opened /plants and then used Playwright browser_route so that **/api/journal* returned 200 application/json. (1) With the body "unexpected text" (a JSON string), clicking the Journal nav link (a client-side fetch) rendered '15 entries' and 15 cards that only show '–', with no plant name, no text and no error. The 15 cards are the 15 characters of the string, iterated because entries.length is truthy. (2) With the body {"items":[]}, the plant detail page /plants/1 Journal section showed 'No journal entries yet', while its header still said '2 entries' (that count comes from the plant record). No load error appeared in either case. Code: pages/journal.vue:19 and pages/plants/[id].vue:15 pass the useApiFetch<JournalEntry[]> result straight to the template, and nothing checks Array.isArray. useApiFetch has no transform or validation, so an unreadable response is shown as fake entries or as an empty journal instead of the existing 'Could not load the journal.' error.

plant-journal/nul-body-500.sentence: POST/PUT /api/journal with a body starting with or consisting of a NUL character returns 500 because the SQLite length CHECK fails with an unhandled IntegrityError.
plant-journal/nul-body-500.evidence: Logged in via POST /api/auth/login as the demo user and sent the requests with curl. POST /api/journal {plant_id:1, entry_on:'2026-01-01'} with body '\u0000x', '\u0000' and '\u0000abc' each returned 'Internal Server Error' [500]. body 'x\u0000y' returned 201 (NUL in the middle is accepted). Then PUT /api/journal/4 with body '\u0000x' also returned 500. The test entry was deleted afterwards (204). Code: schemas.JournalEntryIn checks only min_length=1/max_length=500 in Pydantic, but db.py has CHECK (length(body) BETWEEN 1 AND 500). SQLite length() on TEXT counts characters only up to the first NUL, so a leading NUL makes the length 0 and the CHECK fails. routers/journal.py does not catch sqlite3.IntegrityError and there is no exception handler, so the server returns an unhandled 500 instead of a 4xx validation error.

plant-journal/null-fields-rendered-raw.sentence: When API fields are null, the plants list shows 'null journal entries' and journal feed items render with empty plant name and body and only '–' as date.
plant-journal/null-fields-rendered-raw.evidence: I reproduced it only with mocked responses. After signing in as demo@example.com, I used Playwright page.route to rewrite the real GET /api/plants response so that journal_count was null for the first plant, and the plant card then read 'null journal entries'. I also rewrote GET /api/journal so the first entry had plant_name, body and entry_on set to null. That feed item showed an empty plant link, an empty body and '–' for the date ('3 entries\n\n–'). The real API cannot send these nulls. journal_count comes from COUNT(DISTINCT j.id), which is never NULL in SQLite (0 when there are no rows). JournalEntryOut and PlantOut (schemas.py) declare plant_name: str, body: str, entry_on: date and journal_count: int as required, non-optional fields used as response_model, so FastAPI would fail rather than send null. The journal_entries columns are NOT NULL, and plants.name is NOT NULL with an inner JOIN. The frontend types (types/api.ts) declare these fields non-nullable, and the new code handles them the same way the app already handles existing fields such as bed_name and harvest_grams. formatDate's '–' fallback for a missing date is existing, deliberate behaviour. Without mocking, the real app showed correct values ('1 journal entry', '2 journal entries', real plant names and dates). The odd output only appears when the server breaks its own typed contract, which no real request can make it do.

plant-journal/out-of-range-id-500.sentence: Journal endpoints (POST plant_id, GET ?plant_id=, PUT/DELETE /api/journal/{id}) return 500 instead of 4xx when given integers larger than 64 bits.
plant-journal/out-of-range-id-500.evidence: Logged in as the demo user and called the API with curl. With id 99999999999999999999 and with 9223372036854775808 (2^63), all four journal calls returned 'Internal Server Error' [500]: POST /api/journal {plant_id:N,entry_on:2026-01-01,body:x}, GET /api/journal?plant_id=N, PUT /api/journal/N and DELETE /api/journal/N. With 9223372036854775807 (the largest 64-bit integer) the same calls gave the correct answers: 422 'Choose an existing plant.', 200 [], 404, 404. Code: in routers/journal.py and schemas.py the ids are only checked with gt=0 and have no upper limit, so Python's sqlite3 raises OverflowError when it binds the value, and nothing turns that into a 4xx. Note: the existing GET /api/plants/99999999999999999999 also returns 500, so this weakness was already in the app before the change. The new journal endpoints copy it rather than add it. Only hand-made API requests can hit this; the UI cannot send such ids, and no data is lost.

plant-journal/plant-journal-capped-500.sentence: The plant detail journal fetches at most 500 entries with no paging or notice, so older entries are unreachable while the badge shows the full count.
plant-journal/plant-journal-capped-500.evidence: Code: [id].vue fetches useApiFetch('/journal', {query:{plant_id, limit: 500}}) and the backend caps limit at le=500 (limit=501 returns 422), with no offset/cursor parameter. Reproduced: through the API I created plant 'Cap Test Plant' (id 4) and gave it 503 journal entries dated 2020-01-02..2021-05-19 ('Entry number 1'..'Entry number 503'). GET /api/plants/4 returned journal_count=503. In the browser I signed in as the demo user and opened /plants/4: the Journal badge read '503 entries', but the list showed exactly 500 items. The last one was '5 Jan 2020 Entry number 4', so entries 1-3 (the oldest) were missing. There was no 'show more'/pagination control and no 'showing N of M' notice. Those 3 entries cannot be seen, edited or deleted from the plant page. The Journal page only shows the latest entries, so it doesn't reach them either. Afterwards I deleted the test plant.

plant-journal/search-box-not-synced-with.sentence: On /journal?q=tom, clicking Journal in the nav or using back/forward changes the URL but the search box and results keep the old query.
plant-journal/search-box-not-synced-with.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /journal?q=tom: the search box said 'tom' and the page showed '2 entries match'. Clicked 'Journal' in the top nav: the URL changed to /journal, but the box still said 'tom' and the page still showed '2 entries match' with 2 items. Then I cleared the search (URL /journal, 3 entries) and pressed browser back: the URL went to /journal?q=tom, but the box stayed empty and the page showed '3 entries' (unfiltered). Code cause: in pages/journal.vue, `search` is read from route.query.q only once when the page is created. A watcher pushes search -> URL, but nothing watches route.query.q, and Nuxt reuses the page component when only the query changes. So the URL and the UI drift apart.

plant-journal/search-case-sensitive-non-.sentence: Journal search uses plain SQLite LIKE, so searching 'église' does not match an entry containing 'Église'.
plant-journal/search-case-sensitive-non-.evidence: Logged in via POST /api/auth/login as the demo user and created a journal entry on plant 2 (Courgette) with the body 'Visited the Église garden ZZQTEST'. GET /api/journal?q=ZZQTEST and ?q=zzqtest both returned it, so ASCII search ignores case. ?q=Église returned it, but ?q=église returned []. backend/routers/journal.py:45 uses plain 'j.body LIKE ? ESCAPE' with no lower()/casefold, custom function or collation. SQLite LIKE ignores case only for ASCII letters. frontend/app/pages/journal.vue sends the search box value straight to this API as q, so the Journal page search behaves the same way. As a result, search ignores case for ASCII text but not for accented letters, which a user would not expect. The test entry was deleted afterwards.

plant-journal/search-no-debounce-stale-r.sentence: The /journal search fires a request per keystroke with no debounce, so on a slow network an older response can overwrite newer results.
plant-journal/search-no-debounce-stale-r.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /journal. Used page.route so the response for the first keystroke (q=l, which matches 2 entries) was held back by 4s while the next one (q=le, which matches 1 entry, Lettuce) went through at once. Then I typed 'le' with 150ms between keys. Each keystroke did send its own request (there is no debounce). But when q=le was sent, Nuxt's useFetch (dedupe 'cancel' by default) aborted the q=l request: the browser logged a requestfailed for q=l with net::ERR_ABORTED. The page showed '1 entry match' (Lettuce) 1s after typing and still showed it 6s later, after the delayed q=l response was released. Stale results never replaced the newer ones. Having no debounce only means a few extra small requests, and the request did not ask for a debounce.

plant-journal/search-results-capped-50-m.sentence: A /journal search matching more than 50 entries says '50 entries match' and silently drops the rest.
plant-journal/search-results-capped-50-m.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and created 60 journal entries on Courgette through the API, each containing 'zqxtoken'. GET /api/journal?q=zqxtoken&limit=500 returned all 60. In the browser, /journal?q=zqxtoken showed the count text '50 entries match' and listed exactly 50 items. Nothing said the list was cut short, and there was no 'show more' or 'first 50' text, so 10 matching entries were missing without any sign. The code agrees: journal.vue sends limit=LATEST_LIMIT (50) with searches too, and when searching, resultText prints only the length of the returned list ('N entries match'). It only labels the cap ('Latest 50 entries') when there is no search. The backend LIMITs to the requested value. So the search shows a wrong total and quietly hides matches. The report's side point about the plant page loading at most 500 entries was not tested. The test entries were deleted afterwards.

plant-journal/today-timezone-mismatch.sentence: The form defaults and limits the date to the browser's local today but the server validates against its own date.today(), so a user in a timezone ahead of the server gets 'Journal date cannot be in the future.' for today.
plant-journal/today-timezone-mismatch.evidence: Server time was Thu 2026-11-12 19:39 CET. In Playwright I opened a new browser context with timezoneId 'Pacific/Kiritimati' (UTC+14), where the browser's time was Fri 2026-11-13 08:39. I signed in as demo@example.com and opened /plants/2. The journal form's date input defaulted to value=2026-11-13 with max=2026-11-13, so the client's own check passes. I typed 'TZ test entry today' and clicked Add entry. The request POST /api/journal {entry_on:'2026-11-13', body:'TZ test entry today', plant_id:2} returned 422 {msg:'Value error, Journal date cannot be in the future.'} and the form showed 'Entry on: Journal date cannot be in the future.' Cause: schemas.JournalEntryIn.not_in_future compares with the server's date.today() (backend/schemas.py:113-115), while JournalEntryForm.vue takes its default and max from todayIso() in browser local time (utils/format.ts:26). The form offers a date as the default and the maximum, then the server refuses it. A gardener ahead of the server's timezone cannot log an entry for their own today for part of each day. Workaround: pick yesterday's date. Note: the existing harvest validator (schemas.py:88) uses the same pattern, so the convention predates this change, but it still breaks the new journal feature's default path.

watering-log/beds-load-error-silent-in-f.sentence: On /waterings, when GET /api/beds fails the error is ignored and the Bed select silently offers only 'All beds' with no message or retry.
watering-log/beds-load-error-silent-in-f.evidence: Signed in as the demo user, used Playwright to make /api/beds return 500, opened the dashboard, then clicked the Waterings link (client-side navigation). The #watering-bed select had only ['All beds'], there were no [role=alert] elements, and the main text was 'Bed / All beds / 2 waterings, 14 L in total' plus the table, with no error and no retry. With the route removed, the select shows 'All beds', 'North bed', 'Shade corner'. (Loading /waterings directly is server-rendered, so the browser route did not affect it.) The code in frontend/app/pages/waterings.vue matches: `const { data: beds } = bedsResult` never reads the error, and the options come from `beds ?? []`, whereas wateringsError is shown in an AlertMessage. So filtering by bed is silently impossible.

watering-log/boolean-bed-id-accepted.sentence: POST /api/waterings with bed_id set to JSON true returns 201 and records the watering on bed 1 instead of a 422.
watering-log/boolean-bed-id-accepted.evidence: Signed in via POST /api/auth/login with the demo credentials, then POST /api/waterings with body {"bed_id":true}. Got HTTP 201 and {"id":3,"bed_id":1,"bed_name":"North bed","watered_on":"2026-11-12","watered_at":"2026-11-12 18:53:25","litres":null}, so a watering was saved on bed 1. For comparison, {"bed_id":"abc"} returns 422 int_parsing. The cause is that WateringIn.bed_id is declared as `int = Field(gt=0)` under pydantic's lax mode with no strict setting, so JSON true is turned into 1. I deleted the test watering afterwards (DELETE returned 204).

watering-log/boolean-litres-accepted.sentence: POST /api/waterings with litres set to JSON true returns 201 and stores 1 litre instead of a 422.
watering-log/boolean-litres-accepted.evidence: Logged in via POST /api/auth/login with the demo credentials, then sent POST /api/waterings {"bed_id":1,"litres":true}. Got 201 {"id":3,"bed_id":1,"bed_name":"North bed",...,"litres":1.0}, and GET /api/waterings?bed_id=1 listed it as 1.0 L. For comparison, litres:false returned 422 only because of the gt=0 rule (Pydantic coerced it to 0), and the string "5" was also accepted as 5.0. Cause: WateringIn in backend/schemas.py is a StrictModel that sets only extra='forbid', not strict=True, so Pydantic's lax mode turns a JSON boolean into a float. A boolean isn't a valid amount of litres, so a 422 is the expected result. The UI form sends numbers, so in practice only direct API clients hit this. I deleted the test rows afterwards.

watering-log/create-not-idempotent.sentence: POST /api/waterings has no idempotency key or dedupe, so retrying 'Water now' or 'Save watering' after a lost or timed-out response records a duplicate watering.
watering-log/create-not-idempotent.evidence: Reproduced the mechanics: signed in as demo user, on /beds used Playwright route to let the first POST /api/waterings reach the server (route.fetch) and then abort the response as timed out; clicked 'Water now' on North bed, then clicked again. GET /api/waterings went from 2 to 4 rows (ids 3 and 4, 18:48:24 and 18:48:25), second click showed 'Watered North bed.'. Code: create_watering always INSERTs, frontend sends no key. However, this is plain non-idempotent POST behaviour consistent with the rest of the app: no create endpoint in the codebase (beds, plants, harvests, tasks) has idempotency keys or dedupe (grep finds none), and the request does not ask for it. Content-based dedupe would be wrong because watering the same bed twice, even close together, is a legitimate action. The button is disabled while a request is in flight, so double clicks are prevented, and an accidental duplicate shows up on the waterings page where it can be deleted. A duplicate only happens on the rare case of a response lost after commit followed by a manual retry, which is a general hardening idea, not a defect in this change.

watering-log/dashboard-malformed-never-r.sentence: When the dashboard's recent-waterings response is a malformed non-list (e.g. a string), the table renders rows reading 'Never' with blank bed and '–' amount and no error.
watering-log/dashboard-malformed-never-r.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /beds. Used Playwright page.route to make GET /api/waterings?limit=5 return 200 application/json with the JSON string "oops bad", then went to the Dashboard with the client-side link. The Recent waterings section showed a table with header WHEN/BED/AMOUNT and 8 rows of 'Never' / (blank) / '–', one row per character of the 8-character string. No AlertMessage or error was shown. Cause in frontend/app/pages/index.vue: the table is rendered under v-else-if="waterings && waterings.length" with v-for over waterings, and nothing checks Array.isArray, so a string passes the check and is iterated by character. formatWatered(undefined, undefined) returns 'Never' and formatLitres(undefined) returns '–'. The user sees made-up watering rows that look like real data instead of the expected 'Could not load recent waterings.' error.

watering-log/dashboard-non-array-shown-e.sentence: When the dashboard's GET /api/waterings?limit=5 returns a non-array object, 'Recent waterings' shows the 'No waterings yet' empty state instead of an error.
watering-log/dashboard-non-array-shown-e.evidence: Signed in as demo@example.com. The real GET /api/waterings?limit=5 returns 200 with 2 waterings (Shade corner 2026-11-05, North bed 2026-11-01). On /beds I added a Playwright route so that request returns 200 application/json {"items":[]}, then clicked the Dashboard nav link (client-side navigation, so the browser makes the fetch). The 'Recent waterings' section showed 'No waterings yet / Use “Water now” on a bed to record one. / Go to beds', and there were no role=alert elements. Code cause: frontend/app/pages/index.vue shows the error only when useFetch sets an error; a truthy non-array object fails `waterings.length` and falls through to `<EmptyState v-else-if="waterings">`. useApiFetch (composables/useApi.ts) does no shape validation. So a malformed response looks like an empty watering log even though waterings exist.

watering-log/delete-retry-404-error.sentence: On /waterings, retrying a Delete whose first request already succeeded returns 404 'Watering not found.' and shows an error instead of being treated as done.
watering-log/delete-retry-404-error.evidence: Reproduced through the API: signed in, created watering 3 with POST /api/waterings, then DELETE /api/waterings/3 returned 204 and a second DELETE returned 404 {"detail":"Watering not found."}. The /waterings page catches the error and shows it in listError, so a retry would show that message. This is the app's existing convention, not something the change introduced: delete_task, delete_harvest, delete_plant and delete_bed on main all look the row up first (raising not_found) before deleting, and the existing pages handle delete errors with the same try/refresh, catch/show-error pattern. The request does not ask for deleting waterings at all, let alone for idempotent deletes. A 404 for a resource that no longer exists is a deliberate, consistent design choice, and reloading the page shows the correct list.

watering-log/double-click-water-now-dupl.sentence: Clicking 'Water now' twice quickly on /beds sends two POSTs before the button disables and records two waterings.
watering-log/double-click-water-now-dupl.evidence: Signed in as the demo user on /beds and tried real input on the North bed 'Water now' button through Playwright, counting POST /api/waterings each time. Each try sent exactly 1 POST: locator.dblclick() (before it, GET /api/waterings returned 2 rows; after it, 3), two parallel page.mouse.click() calls, mouse click followed by a clickCount:2 click, and two Enter presses in parallel on the focused button. In each case the button is disabled (wateringBedId set, Vue re-renders before the next input event) before a second click is handled. The only way I got two POSTs and duplicate rows (ids 4 and 5, both North bed at 2026-11-12 18:55:03) was calling HTMLElement.click() twice synchronously in one page.evaluate. That puts two click events in one JS task, which no mouse or keyboard input can do. The code has no synchronous in-flight guard (recordWatering only sets a ref that drives :disabled) and no idempotency key. But the app never retries automatically, and the reported user action (a quick double click) records one watering. The duplicate needs synthetic same-tick events, so following the reports with real input did not reproduce it.

watering-log/filter-late-response-race.sentence: On /waterings, quickly switching the bed filter on a slow connection may let an earlier response overwrite the newer filter's results because there is no request ordering.
watering-log/filter-late-response-race.evidence: Signed in and opened /waterings (beds: North bed id 1, Shade corner id 2). Using Playwright page.route I delayed GET /api/waterings?bed_id=1 by 4s and bed_id=2 by 0.3s, then switched the Bed filter to North bed and 150ms later to Shade corner. The bed_id=2 response arrived first and the bed_id=1 response arrived about 4s later. After both had arrived the list still showed only Shade corner ('1 watering, 4 L in total'), the select read 2 and the URL was ?bed_id=2. In a second run I delayed the unfiltered 'All beds' request by 4s, then switched to North bed. Again the late response arrived last and the list correctly stayed on North bed only ('1 watering, 10 L in total'). The page uses Nuxt 4 useFetch with a reactive query, so the request key changes with the filter and data always follows the current key. A stale response for an old key never replaces what is shown. The report itself was code review only.

watering-log/filter-not-synced-from-url.sentence: On /waterings the bed filter is read from the URL only once, so going from /waterings?bed=N to /waterings via the nav link or Back keeps the old bed selected and the list filtered.
watering-log/filter-not-synced-from-url.evidence: Signed in as the demo user. /waterings with no filter showed 2 rows (5 Nov Shade corner 4 L, 1 Nov North bed 10 L) and the select was empty ('All beds'). Then I loaded /waterings?bed=2, which showed select=2 and only the Shade corner row. Next I clicked the 'Waterings' link in the nav. The URL became http://localhost:3793/waterings, but the select stayed at value 2 and only the Shade corner row was listed, so the URL and the page state disagree. The code agrees: in frontend/app/pages/waterings.vue, bedFilter = ref(route.query.bed) is read once at setup. Only bedFilter->router.replace is watched; nothing watches route.query to update bedFilter, so query changes on the same route (nav link, Back/Forward) are ignored.

watering-log/huge-int-id-500.sentence: Watering endpoints (POST bed_id, GET ?bed_id=, DELETE /{id}) return 500 instead of 4xx for integers beyond 64 bits because SQLite overflows.
watering-log/huge-int-id-500.evidence: Signed in as demo via POST /api/auth/login, then curl with the session cookie against the running API: POST /api/waterings {"bed_id":99999999999999999999,"litres":2} -> 'Internal Server Error' 500; GET /api/waterings?bed_id=99999999999999999999 -> 500; DELETE /api/waterings/99999999999999999999 -> 500; DELETE /api/waterings/9223372036854775808 (2^63) -> 500, while 9223372036854775807 -> 404 'Watering not found.' Code: routers/waterings.py and schemas.WateringIn declare bed_id/watering_id as int (gt=0) with no upper bound, so sqlite3 raises OverflowError when binding the value. Expected 422/404. Note: the existing DELETE /api/beds/{huge} also returns 500, so the pattern is older than this change, but the new watering endpoints have it too. Impact is limited to hand-crafted or edited URLs/requests.

watering-log/hung-filter-stale-rows.sentence: On /waterings, when the request for a newly chosen bed filter hangs, the page stays on 'Loading waterings…' and keeps listing other beds' rows under the selected bed.
watering-log/hung-filter-stale-rows.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /waterings. The unfiltered list showed 2 rows: '5 Nov 2026 Shade corner 4 L' and '1 Nov 2026 North bed 10 L'. Then I used Playwright page.route to make GET /api/waterings?bed_id=... hang and picked 'Shade corner' (value 2). The URL changed to /waterings?bed=2 and the select showed value 2. 13 s later the results line still said 'Loading waterings…', there were no alerts or errors, and the table still showed both old rows, including the North bed row with its Delete button enabled, under the Shade corner filter. The cause is in frontend/app/pages/waterings.vue: the table renders whenever `waterings` holds data, even while status is 'pending'. Nothing hides or marks the old rows (no aria-busy, no dimming), and useApiFetch sets no timeout, so a request that never answers never becomes an error and there is no retry.

watering-log/invalid-bed-query-raw-valid.sentence: Opening /waterings?bed=abc shows the raw backend validation text 'Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer...' with a select that does not match the URL.
watering-log/invalid-bed-query-raw-valid.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened http://localhost:3793/waterings?bed=abc. The page showed an alert with the raw FastAPI/pydantic text "Query.bed id: Input should be a valid integer, unable to parse string as an integer". The Bed combobox had no option selected (options were All beds / North bed / Shade corner, none matching 'abc'), a 'Clear filter' button appeared, and no list or empty state was shown. Cause in the code: frontend/app/pages/waterings.vue copies route.query.bed into bedFilter and sends it as bed_id without checking it, and backend routers/waterings.py declares bed_id: int with gt=0, so the backend returns a 422 whose detail apiErrorMessage shows word for word. A stale or edited link leaves the user with a technical error and a filter control that doesn't match it, instead of the bad filter being ignored or a friendly message.

watering-log/long-bed-name-table-overflo.sentence: At 375px, a long unbroken bed name makes the watering tables on /waterings and the dashboard wider than the viewport, causing horizontal scrolling.
watering-log/long-bed-name-table-overflo.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and created a bed whose name was 60 'A' characters with no spaces (60 is the maximum the schema allows). Recorded a 12.5 L watering for it through POST /api/waterings, then loaded the pages at a 375x800 viewport. On /waterings, document.documentElement.scrollWidth was 869 against a clientWidth of 375, and the table was 836px wide. On the dashboard (/), scrollWidth was 784 and the Recent waterings table was 751px wide. Both pages scroll sideways. main.css has no overflow-wrap or word-break rules, and neither table sits in a scroll container. A gardener's own bed name breaks the mobile layout of both new watering views. Afterwards I deleted the test bed.

watering-log/malformed-watering-fields-r.sentence: Waterings whose fields are null or malformed render as-is on /waterings and the dashboard (e.g. 'Never', blank bed, 'x L', raw 'garbage' date) instead of placeholders.
watering-log/malformed-watering-fields-r.evidence: Reproduced in the browser: signed in as the demo user, mocked GET /api/waterings with page.route to return [{id:1,bed_id:1,bed_name:null,watered_on:null,watered_at:'garbage',litres:'x'},{id:2,...all null}], then went to /waterings and the dashboard by client-side navigation (on a full page load the server renders the page and the mock is skipped). /waterings rows: 'garbage\t\tx L\tDelete watering of' and 'Never\t\t–\tDelete watering of'; the dashboard showed the same. So the rendering the reports describe does happen. But the real backend cannot send this data. WateringOut (backend/schemas.py:146) declares bed_name: str, watered_on: date (required) and litres: float | None, and FastAPI validates responses against it. The list query uses an inner JOIN on beds (routers/waterings.py:18-20), and waterings.bed_id is NOT NULL with ON DELETE RESTRICT (db.py:38), so bed_name and watered_on are always present and litres is a number or null. Null litres already shows '–'. A bad date showing raw text matches how the existing formatDate/formatDateTime helpers treat bad values elsewhere in the app. The request does not ask the client to guard against payloads that break the API contract. The output only appears with a hand-made response that the server would reject, so it is not a defect a user could hit.

watering-log/no-request-timeout.sentence: Watering API calls have no timeout, so when the server hangs, 'Water now'/'Save watering' stay disabled on 'Watering…'/'Saving…' and lists stay loading indefinitely instead of failing after 10 s.
watering-log/no-request-timeout.evidence: Reproduced the behaviour: signed in as the demo user, opened /beds, used Playwright page.route to make **/api/waterings** hang (never answer), then clicked 'Water now' on 'North bed'. After 15 s the button still read 'Watering…', was disabled, and no error was shown. But this is how the whole app has always worked, not something this change got wrong. (1) The request says nothing about timeouts, and the '10 s' expectation in the reports doesn't appear in the request, the specs (.rough-ride/specs/request.txt) or anywhere in the code. (2) frontend/app/composables/useApi.ts is unchanged by the diff (git diff main --stat doesn't list it); useApiClient/useApiFetch never set a timeout, and a grep for timeout/AbortSignal across the app finds nothing. Every existing API call (beds, plants, etc.) behaves the same way when the server hangs. (3) The new watering code uses the existing shared client in the usual way, and its try/catch does show an error (apiErrorMessage -> 'The garden server could not be reached.') when a request actually fails. Adding a client-wide timeout would be a reasonable improvement, but this feature didn't ask for one and the change didn't remove one.

watering-log/nonfinite-litres-500.sentence: POST /api/waterings with litres NaN, Infinity or an overflowing number like 1e309 returns 500 instead of a 422 validation error.
watering-log/nonfinite-litres-500.evidence: Signed in through POST /api/auth/login as the demo user, then sent POST /api/waterings with {"bed_id":1,"litres":X,"watered_on":"2026-11-01"}. For X = NaN, Infinity, -Infinity and 1e309, the API returned 'HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error' with a plain-text 'Internal Server Error' body. As controls, litres 1e308 returned a 422 less_than_equal validation error and litres 5 returned 201. The failing requests inserted no rows. I deleted the control row I created (id 3). Cause: WateringIn.litres is declared as float with gt=0 and le=10000. The 'before' validator does not reject non-finite values, and the app has no custom validation-error handler. So pydantic rejects the value, but the 422 response that echoes the input (nan/inf) can't be serialised and the server crashes. The API should return 422 for bad input, not 500.

watering-log/refresh-failure-replaces-be.sentence: On /beds, if GET /api/beds fails after a successful 'Water now', the bed list and success notice are replaced by 'Could not load beds.' with no retry.
watering-log/refresh-failure-replaces-be.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened /beds, which showed 2 beds (North bed, Shade corner). Used Playwright to make GET **/api/beds return 500 (plain text body), then clicked 'Water now' on Shade corner. POST /api/waterings succeeded: the API's watering count went 3 -> 4. The main area then read only 'Beds / Add a bed form / All beds / Could not load beds.'. Both bed cards, the 'Watered Shade corner.' success notice and every Water now/Edit/Delete button were gone. The only button left was 'Add bed', so there was no retry. An earlier run with a JSON {detail:'boom'} 500 did the same thing (count 2 -> 3, list replaced by 'boom'). Cause in the code: recordWatering in frontend/app/pages/beds.vue awaits refresh() after the POST. A failed refresh clears `beds` (useFetch resets data on error) and sets loadError. The template renders the list only `v-if="beds && beds.length"`, and the success notice is drawn inside each bed card, so both disappear. The user sees a failure even though the watering was saved, and the page has to be reloaded to recover.

watering-log/shared-watering-busy-state.sentence: On /beds a single shared wateringBedId/notice/error state means starting 'Water now' on a second bed re-enables the first bed's button mid-request, allowing duplicate waterings and lost messages.
watering-log/shared-watering-busy-state.evidence: Signed in as the demo user on /beds. Used page.route to hold the first POST /api/waterings and let later ones go through. Clicked 'Water now' on North bed: its button showed 'Watering…' and was disabled. Clicked 'Water now' on Shade corner, which succeeded ('Watered Shade corner.' shown). North bed's button then read 'Water now' and was enabled (disabled=false) while its first POST was still held. Clicked it again, which sent a second POST {bed_id:1}. Captured POSTs: [{bed_id:1},{bed_id:2},{bed_id:1}], so North bed got a duplicate watering. After the held request was released, only 'Watered North bed.' was visible and Shade corner's success notice was gone, because waterNotice is a single shared value. Code cause: beds.vue recordWatering uses one wateringBedId ref (set to bed.id, set to null in finally) and single waterNotice/waterError refs.

watering-log/success-shown-when-refresh-.sentence: On /beds, after 'Water now' succeeds but the follow-up beds refresh fails, the success notice is shown while 'Last watered' stays stale with no error.
watering-log/success-shown-when-refresh-.evidence: Signed in as the demo user, opened /beds, and used Playwright routing to fail GET /api/beds only after the 'Water now' POST /api/waterings returned 201. With a 500 response (detail 'boom'), the bed list went away and the section showed only the error alert 'boom'. With a network abort it showed 'Could not load beds.'. Neither run showed the 'Watered X.' success notice, and no stale 'Last watered' value was presented as current. useFetch's refresh() does not throw, but it sets loadError (shown as an alert at beds.vue:208) and clears data, so the bed cards and the notice inside them are not rendered. The behaviour described in the report did not occur.

watering-log/timezone-today-mismatch.sentence: The server checks future dates and stamps 'Water now' dates using its own time zone while the form uses the browser's today, so users ahead of the server have today's date rejected and dates can disagree with displayed times.
watering-log/timezone-today-mismatch.evidence: Server clock: Thu Nov 12 19:49 CET (18:49 UTC). Opened a Playwright browser context with timezoneId Asia/Tokyo (browser time Fri Nov 13 03:49 JST), signed in as the demo user and went to /beds. Clicked 'Record past watering' on North bed: the date input defaulted to 2026-11-13 with max=2026-11-13 (the browser's today). Entered 3 litres and clicked Save. POST /api/waterings {bed_id:1, watered_on:'2026-11-13', litres:3} returned 422 'Value error, Watering date cannot be in the future.', and the form showed 'Watered on: Watering date cannot be in the future.' So the user's own today, which the form offers by default, is rejected. Cause: schemas.WateringIn.not_in_future compares against the server's date.today(), while the client uses todayIso() in browser local time. Then clicked 'Water now' in the same context: 201 with watered_on '2026-11-12' (server CET date) and watered_at '2026-11-12 18:49:51' (UTC), which is Nov 13 03:49 for this user. The date is stamped from the server's zone, not the user's.

watering-log/tiny-litres-shown-0l.sentence: Litre amounts below 0.005 (e.g. 0.001) are accepted by the form and API but displayed as '0 L' in notices, the dashboard and /waterings.
watering-log/tiny-litres-shown-0l.evidence: Signed in as the demo user. On /beds I opened 'Record past watering' for North bed, entered 0.001 litres and submitted. POST /api/waterings returned 201 with {"litres":0.001}, since the schema only checks gt=0 and the client only checks > 0. The bed card notice then read 'Recorded 0 L on 12 Nov 2026.' /waterings listed the row as '12 Nov 2026 North bed 0 L', and the dashboard's Recent waterings also showed 'North bed 0 L'. The cause is formatLitres (frontend/app/utils/format.ts:40), which uses maximumFractionDigits 2, so a positive amount the app accepted is shown as zero, which contradicts the 'greater than zero' rule. I deleted the test watering (id 3) afterwards.

watering-log/unknown-bed-select-mismatch.sentence: Opening /waterings?bed=<nonexistent id> shows 'No waterings for this bed' while the Bed select shows 'All beds', so filter control and results disagree.
watering-log/unknown-bed-select-mismatch.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and opened http://localhost:3794/waterings?bed=999. The select #watering-bed has options ''/All beds, 1/North bed, 2/Shade corner. Its value reads '' and selectedIndex is -1 (no option matches '999'), so the control does not show any bed filter. Meanwhile the page reads '0 waterings' and 'No waterings for this bed' with 'Clear filter' buttons. Code: waterings.vue sets bedFilter straight from route.query.bed without checking it against the loaded beds, and passes it as bed_id. The backend only filters by w.bed_id and never checks that the bed exists, so it returns []. As a result the filter control and the results disagree, and the bed that doesn't exist is never reported. This only happens with a hand-edited or stale URL, so impact is low.

watering-log/water-now-no-progress-label.sentence: On /beds, clicking 'Water now' while that bed's past-watering form is open disables the button but keeps the label 'Water now' with no 'Watering…' feedback.
watering-log/water-now-no-progress-label.evidence: Signed in as demo user, opened /beds, clicked 'Record past watering' on North bed, then routed POST /api/waterings to hang and clicked 'Water now'. While the request was pending the 'Water now' button was disabled=true but its text stayed 'Water now' (no 'Watering…'). The form's 'Save watering' button instead read 'Saving…' (disabled), even though the user did not submit the form, so the progress feedback goes to the wrong control. After release the button re-enabled as 'Water now'. Cause in beds.vue: the label is `wateringBedId === bed.id && pastFormBedId !== bed.id ? 'Watering…' : 'Water now'`, and the shared wateringBedId drives the form's Saving… label. No reason is shown for the disabled state. The second sample claim (shared wateringBedId/waterError across beds) can be seen in the code but was not tested here.

watering-log/watering-ids-reused.sentence: Watering ids use INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT, so after deleting the newest watering a new one reuses its id and a stale DELETE could remove it.
watering-log/watering-ids-reused.evidence: Reproduced the mechanics through the API: POST /api/waterings twice gave ids 3 and 4; DELETE /waterings/4 -> 204; the next POST returned id 4 again; a repeated (stale) DELETE /waterings/4 -> 204 and removed the new watering. The cause is SQLite's normal rowid behaviour: INTEGER PRIMARY KEY without AUTOINCREMENT reuses the highest id once that row is deleted. But every table in backend/db.py (users, beds, plants, harvests, tasks) is declared the same way, so the waterings table follows the app's existing schema convention; it is not a mistake made in this change. The request does not ask for deleting waterings at all. Only the newest id can come back, and only if a delete for it is replayed after a new watering was recorded (a second stale tab or a retried request) in a single-user app. That is a general design trait of the whole app, not something the user or the request would reject in this change. I removed the test rows afterwards.

watering-log/watering-load-error-no-retr.sentence: When GET /api/waterings fails, the /waterings page and the dashboard 'Recent waterings' section show only an error message with no retry control, so recovery requires a reload or filter change.
watering-log/watering-load-error-no-retr.evidence: Signed in as the demo user and made **/api/waterings* return a plain-text 500. Going to /waterings through the nav showed 'Could not load waterings.' and the main area had no buttons. The dashboard showed 'Recent waterings / All waterings / Could not load recent waterings.' with no retry, and index.vue does not destructure refresh for waterings. So the behaviour is real. But it follows the app's existing convention. In the same run I also failed /api/tasks/upcoming, and the dashboard's existing 'Upcoming tasks' section shows only 'Could not load upcoming tasks.' with no retry either. The main branch has no retry or 'try again' control anywhere in the frontend: tasks.vue, beds.vue and plants/[id].vue all show a plain AlertMessage on load errors, and AlertMessage has no action slot. The request did not ask for retry. The new watering error states are consistent with how the app is designed to handle load errors, so this is not a regression introduced by the change.

watering-log/waterings-page-crash-non-ar.sentence: When GET /api/waterings returns a non-array body, /waterings throws 'waterings.value?.reduce is not a function', navigation stalls or the page sticks on loading, and no error is shown.
watering-log/waterings-page-crash-non-ar.evidence: Signed in as demo user (landed on /beds), routed GET /api/waterings to 200 {"detail":"x"} with Playwright, clicked the 'Waterings' nav link. Uncaught pageerror 'waterings.value?.reduce is not a function'; URL changed to /waterings but document title stayed 'Beds · Garden Log' and the Beds page content stayed on screen (an extra h1 with the raw TypeError text appeared). There was no 'could not load waterings' message and no retry. Cause: frontend/app/pages/waterings.vue:34 totalLitres calls waterings.value?.reduce without an Array.isArray check, and useApiFetch (composables/useApi.ts) does not validate or transform the response, so a non-array 200 body throws while rendering and navigation breaks.

watering-log/year-one-date-accepted.sentence: The past-watering form and POST /api/waterings accept implausible dates such as 0001-01-01, which are saved and listed as '1 Jan 1'.
watering-log/year-one-date-accepted.evidence: API: signed in as the demo user and sent POST /api/waterings {bed_id:1, watered_on:'0001-01-01', litres:5}. It returned 201 with watered_on '0001-01-01', and GET /api/waterings listed the row. UI: on /beds I opened 'Record past watering' for North bed, typed 0001-01-01 and 2 L, and submitted. The date input passed checkValidity(), because it only has max=today and no min. The page confirmed 'Recorded 2 L on 1 Jan 1.' /waterings then showed two '1 Jan 1 North bed' rows, and the totals counted them ('4 waterings, 21 L in total'). Code: the WateringIn validator in backend/schemas.py only refuses future dates; there is no lower bound in the backend or the frontend. An entry from the year 1 is clearly a typo, and it is saved without any reason shown and goes into the log and totals. Because last-watered uses the latest date, the bed's 'Last watered' value was not affected. I deleted my test rows afterwards.
